name: Sticker Materials
seoTitle: Sticker Materials: Vinyl, Clear, Paper, Holographic & More
seoDescription: Compare custom sticker materials: white vinyl, clear film, paper, holographic, metallic and eco-friendly stock. Which lasts outdoors and which costs least.
tagline: The material decides how long a sticker lasts and where it can go. Start here if you know the job but not the stock.
quickAnswer: Sticker material is the face film the design is printed on. Vinyl handles weather and washing for years; paper is the lowest-cost choice for dry indoor labels; clear film shows the surface underneath; holographic and metallic films add shine; recyclable paper and biodegradable films suit brands with a waste policy. Every material here is cut to any shape, from $0.30 per sticker.

sections.h2: How to pick a sticker material in under a minute
sections.html:
Answer three questions. Will the sticker get wet or sit in the sun? Does the surface need to show through? Does it have to shine? The answers point to one of seven stocks, and the wrong answer costs more than any finish choice. A paper label on a cold-brew bottle will wrinkle in the first hour of condensation; a laminated vinyl label on a dry pantry jar is money you did not need to spend.

  1. Wet, outdoors or handled daily: white vinyl, clear vinyl or BOPP.
  2. Dry, indoors, short life or lowest cost: coated or kraft paper.
  3. Needs to disappear on glass or show a surface: clear film.
  4. Needs a rainbow or mirror effect: holographic or metallic film.
  5. Needs to meet a sustainability brief: recyclable paper or biodegradable film.

If two answers conflict, the harsher one wins. A cosmetics jar that lives in a bathroom is a wet environment even though it never goes outside, so it takes our waterproof vinyl stickers, not paper.

sections.h2: Vinyl, the default for anything that has to survive
sections.html:
White vinyl is a calendered PVC film about 3 mil thick with a permanent acrylic adhesive. It stretches a little, which is why it conforms to the curve of a tumbler or the ribs of a cooler lid without lifting at the edges. Printed CMYK sits on top, and a laminate seals the ink against scratches and dishwasher detergent. Most of what people mean by a "durable sticker" is this stock.

  • Dishwasher and car-wash safe once laminated.
  • Takes a full white backing, so colors stay solid on dark surfaces.
  • Cuts cleanly to logo outlines down to about 0.5 inch.
  • Available with removable adhesive for leases and rentals.
  • Pairs with gloss, matte or spot UV finishes.

The custom vinyl stickers page covers sizes, adhesive choices and the difference between calendered and cast film for vehicle work.

sections.h2: Paper and kraft for dry, indoor and budget jobs
sections.html:
Coated paper prints the sharpest small type of any stock, which is why ingredient panels and barcode labels are almost always paper. It is also the cheapest per piece, so it suits packaging seals, event handouts and anything a customer throws away within a week. Kraft paper gives a brown, slightly fibrous face that reads as handmade and takes black or single-color art especially well.

Paper has two hard limits. It absorbs water, so a cold or steamy environment ruins it, and it tears when peeled, so it cannot be repositioned. Use it where neither matters and you save money on every order. Die cut paper stickers are the shape-cut version for bakery boxes, candle jars and shipping cartons.

Clear vinyl prints your artwork on a transparent face so the glass, bottle or box shows through. Ask for a white ink underlay beneath any color that must stay opaque, otherwise a yellow logo on a green bottle turns olive. Holographic film carries a rainbow diffraction layer under the print; it is a merch and limited-edition material, less suited to small text because the shimmer competes with it. Metallic vinyl has a silver or gold mirror base that you print over, leaving unprinted areas as bare metal for borders, seals and badge effects.

All three take the same cut shapes and finishes as white vinyl. The main decision is where to leave the film unprinted, because that is where the effect lives. Our custom holographic sticker page shows how a 20 to 30 percent unprinted area keeps the shimmer visible without drowning the design.

sections.h2: Eco-friendly stocks and what the claims mean
sections.html: Recyclable paper stickers use an uncoated or lightly coated paper face with a water-based adhesive, so they can go through paper recycling with the box they are stuck to. Biodegradable films are plant-derived and break down in industrial composting, not in a backyard pile. Neither is waterproof in the way vinyl is, and we say so on every quote rather than letting a label fail in the field. The eco-friendly sticker options list the exact stocks, their limits and which finishes stay compatible with recycling.

faqs.q: Which sticker material lasts the longest outdoors?
faqs.a: Laminated white vinyl. Expect three to five years on a vertical surface such as a window or vehicle panel, and about half that on a horizontal surface that collects standing water and direct sun. Clear vinyl, holographic and metallic films sit a year or so behind because their effect layers age faster.

faqs.q: Is vinyl or paper better for product labels?
faqs.a: Paper for dry products on shelves, vinyl for anything refrigerated, used in a bathroom or kitchen, or handled daily. Paper prints finer type and costs less; vinyl survives water and peels off cleanly. Many brands use paper for shipping cartons and vinyl for the product itself.

faqs.q: Can clear stickers be printed with white?
faqs.a: Yes. We print a white ink underlay beneath any area that must stay opaque, then CMYK on top. Without it, colors tint toward whatever surface sits behind the film. You can also leave areas fully clear so the bottle or glass shows through.

faqs.q: Do holographic and metallic stickers work outdoors?
faqs.a: They do, with a laminate, for roughly two to three years. The diffraction and mirror layers fade a little sooner than plain vinyl under direct sun, so they are best on laptops, packaging, merch and shaded signage rather than a south-facing storefront.

faqs.q: What material should I use for cold-brew or beer bottles?
faqs.a: Waterproof vinyl or BOPP with a permanent adhesive and a gloss or matte laminate. Condensation and ice buckets destroy paper within hours. Apply the labels to dry bottles at room temperature and let the adhesive set for 24 hours before chilling.

Not in the way vinyl is. Recyclable paper tolerates light moisture at best, and biodegradable films handle splashes but not immersion or outdoor exposure. If a product is both wet and needs an eco claim, use the biodegradable film indoors and keep it out of refrigerators.

faqs.q: Can I mix materials in one order?
faqs.a: Yes. Many customers order vinyl for the product label and paper for the shipping-box seal in a single quote. Each material is priced on its own run, so mixing does not cost extra beyond the per-material minimum of 100 pieces.

faqs.q: What thickness are your sticker materials?
faqs.a: Vinyl runs about 3 mil (0.003 inch) before laminate and roughly 5 mil after. Paper stocks are 60 to 80 lb text weight. Holographic and metallic films are similar to vinyl. Thickness matters mostly for application on tight curves, where thinner stock conforms better.

faqs.q: Which material is cheapest per sticker?
faqs.a: Coated paper, followed by kraft paper, then white vinyl. Holographic and metallic films cost the most because the base film is pricier. At 500 pieces or more the gap narrows, since setup is a larger share of the cost than the material at small quantities.

faqs.q: Does the material change which finish I can choose?
faqs.a: Gloss, matte and spot UV are available on every stock. Kraft paper is usually left unlaminated to keep its texture; clear vinyl takes gloss by default so the film stays invisible; holographic film takes gloss or matte, where matte softens the shimmer.

faqs.q: How do I get a sample of a material before ordering?
faqs.a: Ask for material swatches on the quote form and tell us the surface you will apply to. We send printed swatches of the stocks you are deciding between so you can test adhesion and look on the real product before the 100-piece run.
